transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess... what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has been all over the place lately. Some weeks I barely touch dinner, just push it around the plate. And then other nights, I'm just standing in the kitchen in the dark, eating crackers and sweets long after everyone else has gone to bed. It’s funny, the kitchen always feels so different at night, you know? Like the hum of the refrigerator is the only thing keeping you company. We got this new fridge last year, stainless steel, and it leaves fingerprints everywhere. I spend half my day just wiping it down with a microfiber cloth. My neighbor, Susan, she told me to use a little olive oil on it, but that just made a greasy mess. Anyway, I don't know why I can't just eat a normal meal at a normal time anymore.
After eating late at night like that, do you ever do anything to try to counteract the food, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, or fasting?

Oh, no, I don't do anything like that. I can't stand throwing up. The last time I was sick like that was when I caught a stomach bug from my niece, Chloe. She's seven, and you know how kids that age are just little germ factories. She came over for Easter and gave it to the whole family. We couldn't even finish the ham. It was a honey-baked one, too, the kind with the thick crunchy glaze on the outside. They have a store over on 4th Street that just sells those hams, which always seemed strange to me. How do they stay in business year-round just selling ham? I guess people buy them for sandwiches in the summer. I used to love a good ham sandwich when I was taking classes at the community college... they had this little deli right across the street from the art history building. The owner always remembered my order. But anyway, no, I don't take laxatives or anything. I just eat the sweets and then go to sleep.
{"intent": "Screen for manic or hypomanic episodes to differentiate mood disorders from primary eating disorders", "question": "Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energized, revved

Oh, definitely. Sometimes I get so revved up I literally cannot sit still. It's like if I stop moving, I'll just crawl right out of my skin. So I'll just go and go... I'll clean all the shelves in the house, or completely rearrange my art supplies. I have this huge wooden box of oil pastels I bought at a garage sale a few years ago. The woman selling them said they belonged to her husband who thought he was going to be the next Bob Ross, you know, with the happy little trees? I love Bob Ross. His voice is just so soothing. Sometimes I leave his show playing on the TV just for background noise while I'm drafting poems or pacing back and forth through the garden. 

The garden is looking a bit overgrown right now, honestly. The tomato plants are just taking over everything. I tried to stake them up with these green plastic ties I found at the hardware store, but the guy there told me I should use twine instead. He was wearing this bright orange apron that was completely covered in paint splatters. I wonder what he was painting. Probably a birdhouse. My grandfather used to build birdhouses out of old fence boards... but anyway, yes, I get very energized like that.
Have you ever experienced the opposite, where you had periods lasting weeks of feeling very down, depressed, or losing interest in things?

Well, yes, I do get like that sometimes. I go through stretches where... I don't know, the whole house just feels gray and heavy. I'll just sit at the kitchen table feeling completely empty, even though nothing terrible has happened that day. It's just this weight. And speaking of the kitchen table, it's this beautiful oak table that my mother gave me when she moved into her condo. She downsized a few years ago because she said the stairs in her old house were getting to be too much for her knees. She had both of them replaced, you know, the knees. The recovery for that was just awful. I had to go over there every day for a month to help her with her physical therapy exercises. They gave her this stretchy rubber band thing to pull on, it was bright purple. Purple used to be my favorite color when I was in middle school, I had my whole bedroom painted lavender. It looked awful in retrospect, like living inside a grape. But yes, I do get very down and lose interest in things for weeks at a time.
During those down periods, was it ever so severe that you were completely unable to work or take care of your daily responsibilities?

Well, yes, it does get that bad sometimes. I mean, I don't go to an office or anything, but I've definitely fallen way behind on my facilitator training. And I do some private blog work, but lately, it's just... I can't seem to organize my thoughts or explain things right. My projects just sit there. It's like trying to untangle a huge knot of yarn. I used to knit all the time, actually. I made this beautiful scarf for my husband, David, a few winters ago. It was a really soft merino wool, dyed this deep forest green. He wore it every day that season. He works over at the bank, the one downtown with the big stone columns out front. Have you seen it? It looks like a Greek temple or something. I always wonder how they keep those columns so clean with all the city smog. They must have a special crew that comes out and power washes them at night while everyone is sleeping. I'm a very light sleeper myself, the slightest noise wakes me up. A garbage truck, a dog barking... our neighbor's dog, a golden retriever named Buster, barks at every squirrel he sees. He's a sweet dog, though, he always brings me his tennis ball when I go out to check the mail. But anyway, yeah, the tension at home has made it really hard to keep up with my normal routines with David, and the blog and training just kind of fell apart.
When you have those times of feeling so revved up and energized, how many days do they typically last?

Well, those energized, overcommitted stretches... they usually last a while. I'd say they've been part of my life for about a year and eight months now, off and on. It's funny how time just slips by like that. Eight months ago was right around the time my sister had her baby shower. We held it at this little tea room downtown, the one with the floral wallpaper and the mismatched china cups. I had a cup that had little blue cornflowers painted all over it. It reminded me of the dish set my grandmother used to keep in her hutch. She never let us eat off them, they were strictly for display. She had this whole collection of ceramic thimbles, too, from all the places she traveled. Paris, Rome, London... I've always wanted to go to London. I read somewhere that it rains there almost every day, which sounds wonderful. I love the smell of rain on hot pavement, it's called petrichor. I learned that word from a crossword puzzle I was doing last Tuesday. I try to do the Sunday crossword every week, but the clues get so tricky toward the bottom right corner. I usually have to ask David for help, but he's been so busy at the bank lately... but yeah, about a year and eight months for those revved-up periods.

{"intent": "Clarify the duration of a single energized episode to differentiate hypomania from mania or shorter mood fluctuations", "question": "When you enter one of those energized stretches, how many days

Oh, you mean just one of those times? I... I don't really count the days. I'm not sure, honestly. Time just gets so blurry when I'm feeling that way. Speaking of time, David bought me this beautiful wall calendar for the kitchen not too long ago. It has these gorgeous pictures of lighthouses from all over the East Coast. I've always loved lighthouses. We went up to Maine once, years ago, and saw the Portland Head Light. It was so incredibly windy that day, my hat blew right off my head and went straight into the water! It was this lovely straw hat with a wide brim, the kind you wear to the beach to keep the sun off your face. My dermatologist is always lecturing me about sun protection, she says you have to wear SPF 50 even when it's cloudy out. Apparently, cloudy days can give you the worst sunburns because you don't feel the heat warning you. I bought this special facial sunscreen that smells like coconuts, it reminds me of being on a tropical vacation... but anyway, no, I really couldn't tell you exactly how many days a single stretch lasts. I just kind of lose track.
During those revved-up, energized periods, did they ever cause serious trouble or disruption in your life or relationships?

Well, it's kind of like what I was saying earlier... about my facilitator training and the private blog work? When I get all revved up like that, I still end up falling way behind. You'd think having all that extra energy would mean I get more done, but my projects and explanations just become so hard to organize. My brain is just going in too many directions at once to make sense of it all. And it definitely causes trouble with David. The tension at home gets pretty high, and it makes it so hard to keep up our normal routines together. 

He likes things to be very predictable and calm, especially after a long day at the bank. He usually likes to cook dinner to unwind, actually. He makes this amazing chicken cacciatore, simmering it for hours with fresh tomatoes and oregano. We used to buy the oregano fresh from this little farmer's market over on 4th street. They had the absolute best produce there, all organic. I remember buying these huge, purple heirloom tomatoes from them once. They were so heavy and juicy, not at all like those pale, hard ones you get at the regular grocery store. The grocery store near us always blasts the air conditioning in the produce section, it's absolutely freezing in there. I always have to bring a cardigan with me, even in the middle of July. July is my least favorite month, honestly, because the humidity just completely ruins my hair... I have naturally wavy hair, and the minute it gets humid, it just turns into a giant ball of frizz. I tried this special anti-frizz serum once that had argan oil in it, but it just made everything look greasy.
During any of those energized periods, were things ever intense enough that you had to be hospitalized or go to the hospital for help?

No, I've never had to go to the hospital for it. I mean, I've never been admitted or anything like that. I did visit a hospital once, though, when my cousin Sarah had her appendix out. That was over at St. Jude's... or was it Mercy General? It's hard to remember, the buildings all look so similar with those sterile white walls and the linoleum floors. I hate the smell of hospitals, it's that mix of bleach and rubbing alcohol. It always makes my stomach turn. I have a very sensitive stomach, actually. I can't eat anything too spicy or greasy. Even a mild salsa gives me terrible heartburn. I usually stick to bland foods, like oatmeal or toast. I love making toast with a little bit of butter and that strawberry preserves we get from the farmer's market. The same one where we get the oregano! They have this little old lady who sells the most amazing homemade jams. She uses real cane sugar, not that high-fructose corn syrup stuff. I read an article once about how bad corn syrup is for you, it's in almost everything nowadays. It's so hard to eat healthy when everything is processed... but no, no hospitalizations for me.

{"intent": "Assess for psychotic symptoms during mood episodes to differentiate mood disorders with psychotic features or schizoaffective disorder from uncomplicated bipolar disorder", "question": "During any of

Well, it's funny you ask that, because... yes. When I'm in one of those really charged, unstoppable stretches, you know, when I'm planning out all my workshops and sleeping very little... that's also when things get a bit strange with the online comments. I start feeling like they're actually coded warnings meant just for me. And sometimes, during those same stretches, I'll hear someone call my name, but there's absolutely no one there. It's so startling when that happens. Speaking of names, my parents almost named me Eleanor instead of my actual name. Eleanor was my great-grandmother's name, and she came over from Ireland in the 1920s. She brought this gorgeous antique tea set with her that my mother still keeps in a glass cabinet in her dining room. It's delicate bone china with these tiny, hand-painted blue flowers all over it. I've always been terrified of breaking it, even when I was a little girl. I was a very clumsy child, honestly. I was always tripping over my own feet and scraping my knees. I had this one pair of roller skates that I absolutely loved, they were bright pink with yellow wheels. I'd skate up and down the driveway for hours until the sun went down. The streetlights in our old neighborhood had this really distinct orange glow to them, they always buzzed a little bit if you stood right underneath them... but yes, during those energized times, the comments feel like warnings and I hear my name.
Have you ever experienced those coded warnings or heard your name when your mood was completely normal, rather than when you were feeling revved up or down?

Yes, actually, I have. There have been several weeks at a time where my mood was just... fine, you know? Not high, not low, just perfectly normal. But even then, I still felt so sure that people online were tracking my garden photos. I post a lot of pictures of my hydrangeas, they're just blooming so beautifully this year. I use this special fertilizer that my neighbor recommended, he swears by it. He has the most amazing lawn on the whole street, not a single weed in sight. He spends hours out there every weekend with this tiny little tool, digging up dandelions by the root. Dandelions are actually edible, you know. You can make tea out of the roots, or put the greens in a salad. I tried it once, but it was a bit too bitter for me. I prefer spinach or arugula. Arugula has that nice peppery bite to it. I like to make a salad with arugula, goat cheese, and toasted walnuts... but yes, even when my mood is normal, I still feel like the garden photos are being tracked, and I still hear those brief remarks when I'm completely alone in the house.

I usually stick to bland foods, like oatmeal or toast. I love making toast with a little bit of butter and that strawberry preserves we get from the farmer's market. The same one where we get the oregano! They have this little old lady who sells the most amazing homemade jams. She uses real cane sugar, not that high-fructose corn syrup stuff. I read an article once about how bad corn syrup is for you, it's in almost everything nowadays. It's so hard to eat healthy when everything is processed... but no, no hospitalizations for me.

patient.answer: Well, it's funny you ask that, because... yes. When I'm in one of those really charged, unstoppable stretches, you know, when I'm planning out all my workshops and sleeping very little... that's also when things get a bit strange with the online comments. I start feeling like they're actually coded warnings meant just for me. And sometimes, during those same stretches, I'll hear someone call my name, but there's absolutely no one there. It's so startling when that happens. Speaking of names, my parents almost named me Eleanor instead of my actual name. Eleanor was my great-grandmother's name, and she came over from Ireland in the 1920s. She brought this gorgeous antique tea set with her that my mother still keeps in a glass cabinet in her dining room. It's delicate bone china with these tiny, hand-painted blue flowers all over it. I've always been terrified of breaking it, even when I was a little girl. I was a very clumsy child, honestly. I was always tripping over my own feet and scraping my knees. I had this one pair of roller skates that I absolutely loved, they were bright pink with yellow wheels. I'd skate up and down the driveway for hours until the sun went down. The streetlights in our old neighborhood had this really distinct orange glow to them, they always buzzed a little bit if you stood right underneath them... but yes, during those energized times, the comments feel like warnings and I hear my name.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms occur in the absence of mood episodes to differentiate schizoaffective disorder from bipolar disorder with psychotic features
doctor.question: Have you ever experienced those coded warnings or heard your name when your mood was completely normal, rather than when you were feeling revved up or down?

patient.answer: Yes, actually, I have. There have been several weeks at a time where my mood was just... fine, you know? Not high, not low, just perfectly normal. But even then, I still felt so sure that people online were tracking my garden photos. I post a lot of pictures of my hydrangeas, they're just blooming so beautifully this year. I use this special fertilizer that my neighbor recommended, he swears by it. He has the most amazing lawn on the whole street, not a single weed in sight. He spends hours out there every weekend with this tiny little tool, digging up dandelions by the root. Dandelions are actually edible, you know. You can make tea out of the roots, or put the greens in a salad. I tried it once, but it was a bit too bitter for me. I prefer spinach or arugula. Arugula has that nice peppery bite to it. I like to make a salad with arugula, goat cheese, and toasted walnuts... but yes, even when my mood is normal, I still feel like the garden photos are being tracked, and I still hear those brief remarks when I'm completely alone in the house.
